preview.author: Matt Jones

pick.text: Romania’s miserable run on the road, coupled with how strong the hosts are on home soil, points towards a Bosnia & Herzegovina win.

preview.synopsis: Bosnia have the stronger home record and three straight H2H wins; the writer backs a Bosnia win.

strengths.home: Second place in Group B4 already secured; one defeat in last nine home games (W5, D3) and never lost at home in League B. Alajbegovic in form; Tabakovic injured.
strengths.away: Beat Poland to stay alive at the bottom; poor on the road, behind at half-time in four of five this cycle, but over 2.5 goals in 5 of last 6. Hagi has won six of eight when scoring; Baluta suspended.

preview.author: Matthew Billon

pick.text: A group which has yet to see any side contest a stalemate could see that record end here given what is at stake for both teams, so backing a draw could prove fruitful.

preview.synopsis: A group-deciding game with no draws yet in the group; the writer expects that to end and picks the draw.

strengths.home: Thrashed Portugal 4-1; need only avoid defeat to reach the last eight; score first in all three wins and strong at Parken. Hojlund scoring before half-time.
strengths.away: Beat Wales 3-1 and won the reverse 3-2; both teams scored in each of their last 13 games; Haaland has 66 goals in 60 games. No fresh injuries.

preview.author: John Pennington

pick.text: It might be worth giving some thought to backing the draw here given how tight both defences have been during this campaign.

preview.synopsis: Two tight defences and a promotion race; the writer suggests the draw.

strengths.home: Three straight wins, one point behind and need victory for promotion; defence has conceded twice, but only two wins in last nine at home. Sallai and Varga back; Vitalis suspended.
strengths.away: Top of the group, unbeaten (W3, D2), none of last ten games had both teams scoring; scored first in 4 of 5 away. Devlin in form; Donley suspended.

preview.author: Alex Bowmer

pick.text: Given Poland’s goal-laden second halves recently, both teams to score after half-time looks a possibility here.

preview.synopsis: Poland need a result but are depleted; Sweden are the H2H side. The writer points to both teams scoring after half-time.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in 7 home games but lost 7 of last 10 UNL games; all last five goals scored after half-time and conceded after the hour. Cash injured, Zielinski out, Kiwior suspended.
strengths.away: Won 8 of last 9 H2Hs; both teams scored in 13 of last 15 games; score early (inside 20 minutes in six of seven). Svensson in form.

preview.author: Ben Olawumi

pick.selection: Ireland to win by one goal could well come to fruition
pick.text: The hosts are no strangers to late heroics, and needing all three points, Ireland to win by one goal could well come to fruition.

preview.synopsis: Ireland need all three points; the writer backs a one-goal Ireland win.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in ten at home (W5, D5) but drew both UNL home games; need a win for second place, draw avoids play-offs. Moylan has 14 goal involvements in 13. No new concerns.
strengths.away: Won the first-ever H2H 1-0; four of five games under 2.5 goals, no goal before the hour yet; Saipi 3 clean sheets in 5. Hodza suspended after a red card.

preview.author: Tomáš Vlasák

pick.text: Georgia’s glaring lack of a cutting edge makes backing under 2.5 goals look like a relatively straightforward selection here.

preview.synopsis: Two low-scoring sides; the writer picks under 2.5 goals.

strengths.home: Three straight defeats, winless (D2, L3) and could be relegated; six of seven games 0-0 at half-hour, only two of last eight had both teams score. Unbeaten in all 12 H2Hs; Yaremchuk scores late.
strengths.away: Lack a cutting edge: last eight games under 2.5 goals, rarely score twice away. Tsitaishvili suspended, Kochorashvili back.

preview.author: Ryan Fisher

pick.text: The odds are heavily stacked in Portugal’s favour, but given their shaky defensive display on Saturday and Wales’ recent home matches, both teams to score looks an obvious selection.

preview.synopsis: Portugal are clear favourites but both defences look leaky; the writer picks both teams to score.

strengths.home: Bottom of the group, 9 losses in 11 UNL games, two wins in last eight at home but both teams scored in six of last seven there. Ampadu suspended, Williams injured; Thomas returns.
strengths.away: Won four of five H2Hs, three without conceding; over 2.5 goals in 7 of last 8 UNL games and defensively shaky in the 4-1 loss to Denmark. Dias and Palhinha banned; Fernandes in form.

preview.author: Aaron Murphy

pick.text: Israel need to go all out for glory, and with Austria playing without pressure, over 2.5 goals looks a likely prospect.

preview.synopsis: Israel must attack and Austria are relaxed; the writer likes over 2.5 goals.

strengths.home: Bottom of Group B3, winless (D3, L2), won one of 11 UNL games; neutral-venue game in Debrecen; conceded 3+ in 11 of last 12 losses. Shlomo suspended, Solomon doubtful.
strengths.away: Promoted already, playing without pressure; led at half-time in six of last nine wins; half of their goals came after the 75th minute. Long injury list incl. Prass.
